newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy products end lower as oil falls sharply.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy products end lower as oil falls sharply.

text.p: CBOT soy product futures closed lower on Tuesday as active fund selling late drove soyoil down by nearly one half the daily trading limit, traders said.
"There was big fund selling. Griffin and Prudential sold it late," said Mark Cermak of O'Connor and Co.
Stops were hit in late dealings which extended the losses in soyoil, traders said.
Bleak soyoil export prospects prompted selling in that market early and news overnight South Korea had passed on a tender for 70,000 tonnes soymeal added to the bearish sentiment, traders added.
"The oil (export) business is very quiet right now. There has been some buying interest in the December positions, but right now it's all under the market," one soyoil trader said.
Crush margins closed higher with January up 0.49 cent per bushel at 61.30. Cash soymeal levels remained high with many crushers reporting supplies booked through December.
Soyoil closed 0.47 to 0.31 cent a lb lower while soymeal closed $2.50 to $0.40 per ton lower.
On the day, Griffin Trading and Smith Barney were sellers of the March soymeal while Refco Inc bought December and January, traders said.

Cargill Inc was on both sides of the January soyoil market while Iowa Grain reportedly sold 500 lots December soyoil. Produce Grain and Continental Grain were light buyers of the January, traders said.
Soyoil volume was estimated at 16,000 contracts, compared with Monday's 17,995. Soymeal volume was pegged at 20,000 contracts against Monday's actual volume of 26,604.
